'''Decipher era''' is the printed-card period of ''Star Wars'' CCG, from [[Premiere Limited]] in December 1995 through [[Theed Palace]] in December 2001.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016121021/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref> The publisher was [[Decipher]] of Norfolk, Virginia. The complete constructed pool is [[Premiere - Theed Palace]] (GEMP '''Decipher Cards Only''', <code>open_no_virtual</code>).

== Products and editions ==

The early expansions developed the original trilogy's characters and settings. [[A New Hope Limited]] added creatures, Epic Events and the Death Star mobile location. [[Cloud City Limited]] explored bounty hunting and carbon-freezing. [[Jabba's Palace Limited]] extended those themes into Jabba's court and the rescue of Han Solo.<ref name="decipher-collection">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The product line also offered ways to begin with fixed cards. The two introductory games supplied decks for both sides. [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] combined eighteen fixed cards with booster packs for sealed-deck play. [[First Anthology]] and [[Second Anthology]] bundled earlier packs with preview cards from forthcoming expansions. [[Enhanced Premiere]] paired a new character-and-weapon card with Premiere packs.<ref name="decipher-collection" />

White-border [[Premiere Unlimited]] followed the black-border base set. [[Revised A New Hope]] and [[Revised Hoth]] combined white borders with changes to game text. [[Special Edition]] introduced side-specific starters and included the revised rulebook and glossary with each deck.<ref name="decipher-collection" />

See [[Translations of SWCCG]] for the Japanese editions published by [[Takara]] and the German and Spanish release programs. The released Japanese expansions and introductory games are listed below.

== Sets ==

Decipher sold booster expansions alongside fixed-card products, sealed-deck boxes and anthology collections. The anthologies introduced preview or premium cards while bundling packs and starters from earlier releases.<ref name="decipher-collection">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

Card counts distinguish new cards, alternate images, foil subsets and game aids. A starter row gives the number of cards in a deck. Random reprints packed with Reflections or premium products do not increase their listed set sizes.<ref name="decipher-collecting">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], collecting catalog, pp. 4–45 and 201–202. The primary release notices for the later dates have not yet been located. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Cancelled and planned sets ===

Decipher announced four further expansions after [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], with the planned dates below.<ref name="decipher-planned">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html After Death Star II], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050307015419id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html Internet Archive].</ref>
The later [[Reflections Gold]] project also remained unreleased. In January 2002, [[Warren Holland]] announced that Lucasfilm had refused a proposed free PDF of 200 approved cards.<ref name="decipher-gold">Warren Holland, [http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Star Wars Reflections Gold Announcement], Decipher (25 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080207033202id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Internet Archive].</ref>
[[Reflections Gold Remastered]] is an independent remastered edition documented alongside the surviving original playtest material on [[Reflections Gold]].

== Organized play ==

Decipher ran six World Championships from 1996 through 2001.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive, 17 August 2023]</ref> Each year's constructed pool was printed sets through the newest expansion.

|}

== End of the era ==

Lucasfilm did not renew Decipher's ''Star Wars'' license at the end of 2001.<ref name="wp" /> Stewardship passed to the [[Players Committee]] in 2002. Successor era: [[Virtual Original]].
